source.title: SOLO: A Single Transformer for Scalable Vision-Language Modeling
source.authors: Yangyi Chen; Xingyao Wang; Hao Peng; Heng Ji

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream-performance predictability with benchmark scores fitted against instruction-fine-tuning token count, rather than measuring held-out language-model cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses standard language-model scaling laws and proposes that SOLO makes such analyses easier, but does not run a parameter/token/compute sweep of held-out pretraining cross-entropy or test a compute-optimal allocation. Its relevant scaling-law fit concerns downstream benchmark performance versus instruction-fine-tuning tokens. It also reports comparisons where similar vision-language or fine-tuning loss accompanies different downstream performance.
record.test_reason: A new setting: a 7B vision-language model. The study fits a Kaplan-style power law to downstream benchmark scores as a function of instruction-fine-tuning tokens (Table 4, R²). It also reports that checkpoints with matched vision-language or fine-tuning loss differ in downstream performance (§5.1, §5.2, §7.1). Both bear on V6. No held-out loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute is run. The R² comparison is partly the authors' architecture pitched against mLLaVA.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SOLO's downstream gains from fine-tuning data fit a power law better than mLLaVA's (higher R²), which they take to mean SOLO allows easier scaling-law analysis. They also find that vision-language pretraining loss and fine-tuning loss do not reliably indicate downstream performance, unlike text-only LMs. The R² values are in-sample fits, not extrapolation tests.
record.recipe_differences: Fits downstream benchmark performance against instruction-fine-tuning token count; it does not reproduce the original language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling experiments or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported fit quality differs between SOLO and mLLAVA and across evaluation benchmarks. The paper also reports downstream-performance differences between checkpoints or variants despite similar loss.

fits_no_version.finding: SOLO shows a higher benchmark improvement per fine-tuning token than mLLaVA on all benchmarks (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unified single-transformer VLMs scale more efficiently with fine-tuning data than encoder-based VLMs.

record.problems: The scaling fit is limited to downstream benchmarks versus instruction-fine-tuning tokens, not held-out language-model cross-entropy or a parameter/compute sweep. The comparison covers SOLO and mLLAVA in this setup; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper reports fit R² but does not report a separate held-out extrapolation test against much larger runs.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result-bearing rows omitted. The paper also reports that SOLO improves benchmark performance per training token relative to mLLAVA (Fig. 8), but this is an improvement-rate comparison rather than a reported prediction test; the downstream fit-quality results are recorded in r1–r12.

untested.parts: No held-out loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-to-large extrapolation. Table 4 R² values are in-sample fits.
No compute-optimal allocation. §7.3 only describes a hypothetical plan.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
The power law is fitted to benchmark score versus fine-tuning tokens, not to loss. Fit quality is reported only as R², with no exponents. No image or video loss scaling is tested.
Scaling across model size or pretraining compute. Whether pretraining loss predicts downstream performance within a fixed recipe. Held-out prediction of larger runs.
Exponents are not reported, and no fitting choices are varied.

missing.what: A further loss/performance mismatch: Stage-2 checkpoints with and without ImageNet data, selected at comparable vision-language loss, differ in downstream performance.
Benchmark performance rises consistently with instruction-fine-tuning steps (MME fluctuates), which is the data behind the Table 4 fits.

record.verdict_notes: This is an architecture and recipe paper; its scaling-law material is secondary and partly promotional (own model vs a comparator). All results come from one 7B model per architecture, with no uncertainty estimates. The system is a VLM, so its bearing on LM-specific versions is indirect.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model cross-entropy power-law sweep over parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
No test of predictions from small runs against runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute comparison or estimate of optimal parameter and token allocation.
No controlled study of depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies vision-language modeling, but does not test whether the claimed cross-entropy power law holds in that modality or other training regimes.

Tests power-law fit quality for downstream benchmarks against instruction-fine-tuning token count and reports loss/performance mismatches; does not test broad downstream predictability across model scales or settings.
Does not test how exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with fitting choices or setup, or whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: mLLAVA

rows.measure: R² of power-law fit to benchmark performance
rows.note: The authors use R² to reflect fit quality and report that SOLO's performance is more predictable than mLLAVA's.
rows.check: In-sample R² from a single fine-tuning run, not an extrapolation test. The study uses it to compare its own architecture with mLLaVA, so read it as fit quality, not predictive validation. An R² of 40.32 is a poor fit.

rows.subject: SOLO (Stage-2-only caption-pretraining checkpoint)
rows.stage_stated: Stage-2 pretraining checkpoint, subsequently instruction fine-tuned for 800 steps
rows.operation_detail: Compare downstream benchmark performance after instruction fine-tuning against the two-stage-pretrained checkpoint selected at comparable vision-language modeling loss.
rows.measure: Downstream benchmark performance across multiple evaluation datasets
rows.baseline: two-stage-pretrained SOLO checkpoint; selected at the same vision-language modeling loss
rows.note: The text says the Stage-2-only checkpoint has lower performance across multiple benchmarks despite comparable selected vision-language loss; exact benchmark values are not stated.
rows.check: r13 and r14 are one paired comparison split into two rows. Against V6 (loss predicts downstream performance), equal loss of 2.1 gave different downstream scores, so the effect is absent. Values are figure-only (Fig. 5a).

rows.subject: SOLO (ImageNet plus caption-pretraining checkpoint)
rows.stage_stated: Two-stage pretraining checkpoint, subsequently instruction fine-tuned for 800 steps
rows.operation_detail: Compare downstream benchmark performance after instruction fine-tuning against the Stage-2-only checkpoint selected at comparable vision-language modeling loss.
rows.measure: Downstream benchmark performance across multiple evaluation datasets
rows.baseline: Stage-2-only caption-pretraining checkpoint; selected at the same vision-language modeling loss
rows.note: The text says the two-stage-pretrained checkpoint performs better across multiple benchmarks; exact benchmark values are not stated.
rows.check: Duplicate of r13's comparison. 'Observed' describes recipe superiority, not the V6 effect. Relative to V6, loss failed to predict performance.

rows.subject: SOLO (learning rate 1e-4)
rows.operation_detail: Compare downstream benchmarks for a variant trained with a different learning rate against the prescribed recipe variant.
rows.measure: Downstream benchmark performance; the paper reports significant differences despite similar instruction-fine-tuning loss and training behavior
rows.baseline: SOLO variant using the prescribed learning rate 1e-5
rows.note: The authors state that similar instruction-fine-tuning losses do not reliably indicate task performance; exact benchmark values are not stated.
rows.check: r15 and r16 are one paired comparison (lr 1e-4 vs 1e-5). Similar fine-tuning loss came with significant benchmark differences (Fig. 10). Figure-only. Fine-tuning loss is not pretraining loss.

rows.subject: SOLO (learning rate 1e-5; prescribed recipe)

rows.measure: Downstream benchmark performance; the paper reports significant differences despite similar instruction-fine-tuning loss and training behavior
rows.baseline: SOLO variant trained with learning rate 1e-4
rows.note: The authors state that similar instruction-fine-tuning losses do not reliably indicate task performance; exact benchmark values are not stated.
rows.check: Duplicate of r15's comparison. 'Observed' describes recipe superiority, not the V6 effect.

relationships.condition: SOLO on all six benchmarks, and mLLaVA on MME, SEED, ScienceQA and AI2D; score vs instruction-fine-tuning tokens
relationships.reason: In-sample power-law R² is 83–99 (r2, r3, r4, r6, r7–r12). This comes from a single 7B run with no extrapolation test.
relationships.display_finding: Reported in-sample power-law R² values were 83–99 across the specified benchmarks, based on a single 7B run without an extrapolation test.

relationships.reason: Power-law fits of score vs fine-tuning tokens are poor (R² 40.32 and 62.73; r1, r5), so predictability depends on architecture and benchmark.
relationships.display_finding: Power-law fits against fine-tuning tokens were poor, with reported R² values of 40.32 for MMStar and 62.73 for MathVista.

relationships.condition: Matched vision-language pretraining loss or fine-tuning loss, across recipe variants (initialisation, learning rate)
relationships.reason: Equal loss came with different downstream performance; the authors say loss is not a reliable indicator (r13–r16). The evidence is figure-only, and the comparison is across recipes, not scale.
relationships.display_finding: Different initialization and learning-rate recipes produced different downstream performance at equal pretraining or fine-tuning loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SOLO; downstream benchmarks fitted against instruction-fine-tuning token count
reader_labels.reason: The reported power-law fit R² values are 84.70–98.59 across the six benchmarks, consistent with predictable downstream performance in this tested setting (r7–r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: mLLAVA; downstream benchmarks fitted against instruction-fine-tuning token count
reader_labels.reason: Fit quality varies substantially across benchmarks, including R² values of 40.32 and 62.73, and the authors report SOLO is more predictable overall (r1–r6).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Similar vision-language pretraining loss or instruction-fine-tuning loss, with downstream benchmark evaluation
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports different downstream outcomes for checkpoints with comparable vision-language loss and for variants with similar fine-tuning loss, so loss did not reliably indicate task performance in these comparisons (r13–r16).
